newsitem.title: USA: US emerging mkt bond funds up 28 pct on yr - Lipper.
newsitem.headline: US emerging mkt bond funds up 28 pct on yr - Lipper.

text.p: Emerging market bond funds have posted strong returns year to date, in some cases higher than stock funds, according to Lipper Analytical Services.

Year to date, the sector has returned an average of about 28 percent, while the average U.S. equity fund has gained 12.36 percent, the average taxable bond fund 0.95 percent, and the general municipal debt fund is off 0.59 percent.

Top performers include Phoenix Emerging Market Bond Class A, up 39.93 percent year to date; Morgan Stanley Institutional Emerging Debt Class A, up 35.79 percent; Bear Stearns Emerging Debt Class A, up 29.34 percent; Fidelity New Markets Income, rising 26.73 percent; and Fidelity Advisers Emerging Institutional, gaining 26.16 percent.

Some funds, including Phoenix and Morgan Stanley, have invested almost 20 percent of assets in Russian debt, benefiting from soaring Russian bond prices, according to Lipper. In recent days, some gains have been erased on concerns over the health of Russian president Boris Yeltsin.
Phoenix, the leader in the group, has been fully invested, with 25 percent in Brazil, 19 percent in Russia, 18 percent in Argentina, 13 percent in Mexico, and 12 percent in Venezuela.
